members.docComment:
/**
 * Provides static methods for generating keyboard template blocks from `LabelGKeyboard` definitions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This class generates HTML-like `<g-keyboard>` blocks for the template engine.
 * Requires `LabelGKeyboard` to be set via {@link BlockGKeyboard.label} before using {@link BlockGKeyboard._build}.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // blocks/g-keyboard.ts
 * import { BlockGKeyboard, LabelGKeyboard } from "gramstax";
 *
 * class KeyboardGBlock extends BlockGKeyboard {
 *   static label = class extends LabelGKeyboard {
 *     static backNext = {en: "Back, Next", id: "Kembali, Lanjut"}
 *   }
 *   static backNext = (lang?: string, type?: string) => this._build(`backNext`, lang, type)
 * }
 *
 * // base/page.ts
 * import {KeyboardGBlock} from "~/blocks/g-keyboard"
 * export abstract class PageBase extends CtxCore {
 *   static kbk = KeyboardGBlock
 *   static kbl = KeyboardGBlock.label
 * }
 *
 * // pages/some.ts
 * import {PageBase} from "~/base/page"
 * export class SomePage extends PageBase {
 *   static template = `
 *     <g-base>
 *       ${this.kbk.backNext()}
 *       <g-message>Default message hello world</g-message>
 *     </g-base>
 *     <g-base id="others-id-1">
 *       <g-message>Message from others id 1 with keyboard from base id default</g-message>
 *     </g-base>
 *     <g-base id="others-id-2">
 *       <g-base>${this.kbk.backNext()}</g-base>
 *       <g-message>Message from others id 3 with keyboard in same base</g-message>
 *     </g-base>
 *   `
 * }
 *
 * // understanding example
 * this.kbk.backNext() // will show all language with block template
 * this.kbk.backNext("id") // will show all language only (lang="id") with block template
 * this.kbk.backNext("default") // will show all language only (lang="default" or without lang) with block template
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: BlockGKeyboard

members.docComment:
/**
 * Build keyboard blocks by calling a method from the linked `LabelGKeyboard`.

 * @param key - Method name in LabelGKeyboard. Must exist or throws.

 * @param lang - Target language. If set, returns single language block.

 * @param type - Keyboard type. Values are `"inline"` or `"bottom"`. Defaults to `"inline"`.

 *
 * kbk._build("backNext", "en", "bottom");
 * // => '<g-keyboard type="bottom" lang="en">Back, Next</g-keyboard>'
 * ```

 * @public

/**
 * Extends {@link https://github.com/jaredwray/keyv | Keyv} to provide a unified caching interface
 * with built-in support for memory and Redis storage.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Storage modes:
 * - **Memory mode:** when `url` is `"memory"` (default), uses an in-memory `Map`.
 * - **Redis mode:** when `url` starts with `"redis"`, uses `@keyv/redis` adapter.
 * - **Custom mode:** when `more.forceStore` is provided, uses the custom store.
 *
 * @typeParam V - The type of values stored in the cache.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import { CacheExternal } from "gramstax";
 *
 * // Memory cache (default)
 * const memoryCache = new CacheExternal();
 *
 * // Redis cache
 * const redisCache = new CacheExternal("redis://localhost:6379", 3600000, "s");
 *
 * // With namespace and TTL
 * const cache = new CacheExternal("memory", 60000, "myapp");
 *
 * // Set and get data
 * await cache.set("user:123", { name: "John" });
 * const user = await cache.get("user:123");
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: CacheExternal

 * template rendering, and reply methods.

 *   async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *     const kb = this.inlineKeyboardT([Menu1Page, Menu2Page])
 *     await this.renderText({keyboard: kb})

 * each send owns its copy. Non-`InputFile` values (`string` sources)

/**
 * Deletes a story previously posted on behalf of a managed business account.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Business-connection-only like {@link (Ctx:class).postBusinessStory}: the same
 * `business_connection_id` (with `can_manage_stories`) that posted the
 * story is required. Only presence and the positive-integer `storyId` are
 * fail-fast validated — programmer errors always throw, never fall back.
 *
 * why-not-base: base `Context.deleteStory` takes no `business_connection_id` at all; this deletes under any connection.
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`): failures are
 * classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`,
 * and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`).
 * The original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched after notify+log.
 *
 * @param businessConnectionId - Business connection id (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param storyId - Id of the posted story (or null — throws).
 *
 * @returns `true` on success.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript

 * ```

 */
members.name: deleteBusinessStory

/**
 * Downloads the file attached to the current message.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Requires the `@grammyjs/files` plugin (`hydrateFiles` — mounted by
 * default in Gramstax). Without a path, the file is saved to a
 * temporary location and its path is returned; with a path, the file
 * is written there.
 *
 * **Security:** when `path` is supplied it must not contain NUL bytes
 * or `..` path segments. Absolute or traversal-like values throw — keep
 * downloads inside a dedicated directory (e.g. `os.tmpdir()` or
 * `process.cwd()/downloads`) and pass only a `basename`-derived name
 * when the name comes from user input. The no-arg form (tmp file) is
 * always safe.
 *
 * @param path - Optional destination file path.
 *
 * @returns The saved file path.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: download

/**
 * Build `EphemeralMessageParameters` for Bot API 10.3 ephemeral messages.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Creates the `ephemeral_message_parameters` payload accepted by 13 send*
 * methods plus `sendRichMessage`. Ephemeral messages are short-lived
 * notifications sent directly to a user — they disappear after the user
 * reads (or ignores) them and are not kept in the chat history.
 *
 * The deprecated shim also accepts the pre-10.3 snake_case object
 * `{receiver_user_id, callback_query_id, ...}` and emits a `console.warn`.
 *
 * @param receiverUserId - Target user id, or a legacy object with snake_case keys.
 *
 * @param callbackQueryId - Callback query id that triggered the message (optional).
 *
 * @param replace - Pass `true` to show in place of the original message (optional).
 *
 * @returns The ephemeral parameters object, or `undefined` when no receiver is provided.
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Replace callback query message in place
 * ```typescript
 * async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *   await this.api.sendMessage(this.chatId, `Order received!`, {
 *     ephemeral_message_parameters: this.ephemeralParams(this.from?.id, this.callbackQuery?.id, true)
 *   })
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Legacy 10.2 snake_case object (warns once)
 * ```typescript
 * this.ephemeralParams({receiver_user_id: 123, callback_query_id: `cb_1`})
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: ephemeralParams

/**
 * Page-level hook after a route handler execution.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Always runs after the handler returns (even when the handler returns
 * undefined / null). Ideal for cleanup, analytics, or chained side effects.
 *
 * Useful for:
 * - Recording page visit timestamps
 * - Auto-clearing stale session data
 * - Firing post-processing jobs
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Notify admins of high-value actions
 * async hookAfterRoute() {
 *   if (this.temp.session?.params.amount > 10000) {
 *     await this.api.sendMessage(ADMIN_CHAT_ID, `Large withdrawal: ${this.temp.session.amount}`)
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookAfterRoute

members.docComment:
/**
 * Page-level hook before route handler execution.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Return `false` to **skip only the target route handler** (e.g.
 * `handleFreeText`, `handleCallbackQueryData`, etc.). The rest of the
 * framework is untouched — you can still call `.renderText()`,
 * `.renderCallbackAnswer()`, and other Ctx methods normally inside
 * this hook before returning `false`.
 *
 * In other words: returning `false` does NOT freeze the page — it
 * only prevents one specific handler from running.
 *
 * Useful for:
 * - Per-page cooldown / rate limiting (reply "please wait" then abort)
 * - Precondition checks (reply with redirect page then abort)
 * - Session validity gates
 *
 * @returns `true` to continue (handler runs), `false` to abort (handler skipped).
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Cooldown — reply then abort the handler
 * async hookBeforeRoute() {
 *   const last = await this.cacheSession.get(`${this.from.id}:lastAction`)
 *   if (last && Date.now() - Number(last) < 2000) {
 *     await this.renderCallbackAnswer(true, undefined, `cooldown`) // still works
 *     return false // only skips the target handler
 *   }
 *   await this.cacheSession.set(`${this.from.id}:lastAction`, String(Date.now()))
 *   return true
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // KYC gate — send redirect page then abort
 * async hookBeforeRoute() {
 *   const profile = await this.db.getUser(this.from.id)
 *   if (!profile?.kycVerified) {
 *     await new KycPage(this).showForm() // redirect works
 *     return false // only skips the guarded handler
 *   }
 *   return true
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookBeforeRoute

 *
 * @param AGBaseId - Optional template g-base ID position block keyboard. IMPORTANT: If a `<g-base id="...">` is defined in the template, you must set AGBaseId to the same value. Leaving AGBaseId as undefined in this case will cause errors (for example, keyboard bindings will not work). A common mistake is defining a base ID in the template but not reusing it in the keyboard configuration (or null to use default).

/**
 * Posts a story on behalf of a managed business account.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Business-connection-only: a normal bot cannot call `postBusinessStory` — pass a
 * `business_connection_id` from a `BusinessConnection` update with the
 * `can_manage_stories` right, otherwise the Bot API rejects the call.
 * Thin passthrough otherwise: `content` resolves through `resolveMedia`
 * then uploads (`InputFile` as-is, URLs via `{url}`, `file_id` strings
 * pass through) and only presence, the
 * `photo`/`video` discriminant, and the fixed `active_period` set are
 * fail-fast validated; areas, durations, and captions are adjudicated by
 * the Bot API — programmer errors always throw, never fall back.
 *
 * why-not-base: explicit `businessConnectionId` (base `Context.postStory` uses the current update only) plus local-path `InputFile` resolution and fail-fast validation.
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`): failures are
 * classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`,
 * and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`).
 * There is no degraded fallback content for stories, so after notify+log
 * the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.
 *
 * @param businessConnectionId - Business connection id (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param content - Story content `{type: "photo"|"video", src}` (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param activePeriod - Archive delay in seconds: 21600, 43200, 86400, or 172800 (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param options - Optional extra story fields such as `caption` (or null to omit).
 *
 * @returns The posted story object.

/**
 * Deletes already-sent messages for many recipients in bulk.
 *
 * Template block: none — operates on message ids, reads no template block.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Expiry-cleanup counterpart of the revise fan-out (`renderMedia` with
 * `broadcast.targets`): same
 * checkpoint-first resume (`startFrom`), bounded-concurrency stride lanes
 * (`concurrency`, capped at `10`), pacing (`30`-message free-limit sleep
 * plus optional `chunkSize`/`chunkDelayMs` sleeps with `onProgress`), and
 * retryable separation (`retryable[]` with absolute `index` + `chatId` +
 * `messageId` + `error`, completion order).
 *
 * Per-recipient failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`:
 * `retryable` errors are recorded and the loop continues; `fallback-text`
 * errors only notify (`notifySendError`) and count as failed. A failed
 * delete has no text fallback by design — there is no replacement content
 * to deliver, so no `sendMessage` is attempted on either path.

 * @param params - Delete-fanout params: `targets` stored `{chatId, messageId}` rows to delete, in stable order (checkpoint index = array index) (required); `broadcastOpts` optional broadcast controls (`onProgress`, `startFrom`, `concurrency`, `chunkSize`, `chunkDelayMs`) (or null for defaults; `fallbackEdit` is accepted but ignored — deletes have no resend).

 * @example
 * ```typescript

 */

 *
 * Template block: `<g-invoice>` (read via `getGInvoice`).

 * @remarks
 *
 * Fail-fast validation (`Ctx.assertInvoice`) runs BEFORE any API call on the
 * COMPILED strings — programmer errors always throw, never fall back. The
 * invoice is sent with NO `parse_mode`: the Bot API offers no HTML parsing
 * for invoices.
 *
 * Provider tokens are security-critical and NEVER come from templates: the
 * validator rejects a `provider_token` attribute outright. Resolution order
 * is `options.provider_token` when present, otherwise Telegram Stars
 * (`currency: "XTR"`) sends with no token at all, and any other (fiat)
 * currency without a token throws before any API call.
 *
 * Pre-checkout queries for the sent invoice already route to page handlers
 * via the existing `precheckoutquery` listener — define
 * `handleFreePreCheckoutQuery` (or `handleSessionFreePreCheckoutQuery` in a
 * session flow) on the page and answer with
 * {@link (Ctx:class).answerPreCheckout}. No new routing was added for this.
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`): failures are
 * classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`,
 * and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`).
 * There is no degraded fallback content for invoices, so after notify+log
 * the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched — the `catch` below
 * observes only and never swallows, because swallowing would hide a
 * payment send failure from the caller.

 * @returns The sent invoice message object.

 * ```typescript

 *   const kb = this.inlineKeyboard((k) => k.text("OK", "ok"))

/**
 * Sends or edits a media message with dynamic type selection.
 *
 * Template block: `<g-media>` (read via `getGMedia`).
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Single method for every media send/edit path, folding the former
 * `renderAutoMedia`, `renderEditMedia`, the per-kind reply base, and the
 * broadcast-media / broadcast-edit fan-outs. `mode`
 * resolves the send-versus-edit decision: `auto` (default) edits when
 * `this.callbackQuery` exists, `reply` always sends, `edit` always edits.
 * This is the base method for all media methods. Use specific methods
 * like {@link (Ctx:class).renderPhoto} or {@link (Ctx:class).renderVideo} for simpler usage.
 *
 * Edit-mode semantics for media types that cannot be edited (`voice`,
 * `video_note`, `sticker`, `location`, `contact`) delete the original
 * message and send a new one. Multi-src media groups cannot replace a
 * single message, so supported pipe-delimited media groups also delete the
 * original message and send a new media group.
 *
 * Fail-fast validation (`Ctx.assertMediaPreconditions`, plus
 * `Ctx.assertLocation`/`Ctx.assertContact` in their branches) runs BEFORE
 * any API call — programmer errors always throw, never fall back.
 * Send failures follow `Ctx.classifySendError`: `retryable` rethrows the
 * original error untouched; `fallback-text` best-effort replies with
 * `resolveFallbackText()` (nested failures ignored) and returns it.
 *
 * If the edit itself fails, the fallback behavior is controlled by `fallbackEdit`
 * (default `delete-reply`: deletes the original message and re-sends the same media —
 * the result looks like an in-place edit). The fallback re-send drops `optionsEdit1`/
 * `optionsEdit2` (edit options do not map to reply options) and logs a `log.warn`
 * when non-empty options are dropped; the re-send itself follows
 * `Ctx.classifySendError` via the reply branch (`retryable` rethrows the
 * original error untouched, `fallback-text` replies with fallback text).
 *
 * When `broadcast` is present, multi-recipient fan-out replaces the
 * single-chat path (see {@link IBroadcastSendParams} /
 * {@link IBroadcastReviseParams}): `broadcast.ids` runs the send loop —
 * the media kind is read from the template `<g-media>` block, so `type`
 * may be omitted there and is ignored when supplied — and
 * `broadcast.targets` runs the revise loop. `mode`, `fallbackEdit`, and
 * the `options*` fields do not apply to the send loop.
 *
 * @param params - Media params. See {@link IRenderMediaParams} for field details: `type` the media type (photo, video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location, contact) (omitted only on the broadcast-send path); `keyboard` optional keyboard markup (or null to omit); `data` optional template interpolation data (or null to omit); `AGBaseId` optional template g-base ID position for block media (or null to use default); `mode` send-versus-edit resolution (default `auto`); `options` optional type-specific reply options (or null to omit); `optionsEdit1` optional edit payload / non-editable-type reply options (or null to omit); `optionsEdit2` optional extra `editMessageMedia` call options (or null to omit); `fallbackEdit` fallback when the edit fails (default `delete-reply`); `broadcast` optional broadcast fan-out — `{ids, languageCode, …}` sends, `{targets, broadcastOpts}` revises (or null for a single-chat send/edit).
 *
 * @typeParam T - The media type to send or edit to.
 *
 * @returns The sent or edited message object, or the {@link IBroadcastSendResult}/ {@link IBroadcastEditResult} counts on the broadcast paths.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *   // Automatic reply/edit with content from this.template
 *   await this.renderMedia({type: "photo"})
 *
 *   // Force a new reply even from a callback query
 *   await this.renderMedia({type: "photo", mode: "reply"})
 *
 *   // Broadcast: fan out to many users (kind read from the <g-media> block)
 *   await this.renderMedia({broadcast: {ids: [123456, 789012], languageCode: [`en`, `id`]}})
 *
 *   // Broadcast revise: edit already-sent messages to a new media payload
 *   await this.renderMedia({type: "photo", data: {price: "99"}, broadcast: {targets: sent}})
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Sends or edits a Telegram media group using pipe-delimited `src` values or a `<g-media-group>` block from the page template.
 *
 * Template block: `<g-media-group>` (read via `getGMedia` — the block's `mediaGroup` items).
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Only `photo`, `video`, `audio`, and `document` support Telegram media groups.
 * Omit `type` when the template uses `<g-media-group>` with per-item media types.
 * When the template uses `<g-media-group>` (or null to include all items),
 * only items matching this type are included. When omitted, all items are sent.
 * The first item receives the template caption. Telegram media groups do not support
 * reply markup, so keyboards are ignored for grouped media. Per-item filenames
 * rely on grammy basename auto-guess (no per-item filename override is applied).
 *
 * `mode` resolves the send-versus-edit decision: `auto` (default) edits when
 * `this.callbackQuery` exists, `reply` always sends, `edit` always edits.
 * Media groups cannot be edited in place, so the edit branch always deletes
 * the original message first; when the delete-and-send fails, `fallbackEdit`
 * decides whether to retry the delete and re-send (`delete-reply`, default),
 * re-send without deleting (`reply`), or rethrow (`disable`).
 *
 * Fail-fast validation runs BEFORE any API call (group/item size limits,
 * per-item types, upload sizes, caption length) — programmer errors always
 * throw, never fall back. Send failures follow `Ctx.classifySendError`:
 * `retryable` rethrows the original error untouched; `fallback-text`
 * best-effort replies with `resolveFallbackText()` (nested failures ignored).

 * @param params - Optional media-group params (defaults to `{}`).  * @returns The sent media group messages.

 * @example

 * async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *   await this.renderMediaGroup({type: "photo"}) // only send photo
 *   await this.renderMediaGroup() // send all media group

/**
 * Sends or edits a text message using the page template.
 *
 * Template block: `<g-message>` (read via `getGMessage`).
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Single method for every text send/edit path, folding the former `render`,
 * `renderEdit`, `renderRich`, `renderAuto`, `renderAutoRich`,
 * `renderEditRich`, and `renderBroadcast`. `mode` resolves the
 * send-versus-edit decision: `auto`
 * (default) edits when `this.callbackQuery` exists, `reply` always sends,
 * `edit` always edits.
 *
 * Rich content is chosen at COMPILE time: when the `<g-message>` block
 * contains Telegram Rich HTML tags, the message is sent or edited through
 * `replyWithRichMessage`/`editMessageText` with an `InputRichMessage` payload
 * (Telegram Bot API {@link TemplateEngine.BOT_API_VERSION}) instead of plain
 * HTML text. Rich message limits:
 * - Up to 32,768 UTF-8 characters
 * - Up to 500 blocks
 * - Up to 16 nesting levels
 * - Up to 20 table columns
 *
 * If editing fails (e.g. message too old), the fallback behavior is controlled
 * by `fallbackEdit` (default `delete-reply`: deletes the original message and
 * sends a new reply — the result looks like an in-place edit).
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderMedia`): reply failures are
 * classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`,
 * and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`).
 * Unlike the media paths there is no degraded fallback content for text,
 * so after notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.
 *
 * When `chunkSize` is present (not `undefined`/`null`) the fully-rendered
 * block is sent as sequential reply chunks instead (see the `chunkSize`
 * field of {@link IRenderTextParams}): the keyboard lands ONLY on the last
 * chunk and `mode` does not apply — a multi-message split cannot be edited
 * in place, so the chunked reply wins when both are passed.
 *
 * When `broadcast` is present, the block is SENT to every
 * `broadcast.ids` entry instead (see {@link IBroadcastSendParams}): rich
 * templates through `api.sendRichMessage`, plain templates through
 * `api.sendMessage` with `parse_mode: HTML`; `mode`, `fallbackEdit`, and
 * `chunkSize` do not apply on that path.
 *
 * @param params - Optional render params (defaults to `{}`). See {@link IRenderTextParams} for field details: `keyboard` optional keyboard markup (or null to omit); `data` optional template interpolation data (or null to omit); `AGBaseId` optional template base ID position for block message (or null to use default); `mode` send-versus-edit resolution (default `auto`); `options` optional plain-text reply/edit options (or null to omit); `richOptions` optional `InputRichMessage` fields plus rich send options (or null to omit); `fallbackEdit` fallback when the edit fails (default `delete-reply`); `chunkSize` optional max characters per chunk, selecting the chunked reply path (or null for a single message); `broadcast` optional broadcast fan-out {@link IBroadcastSendParams} (or null for a single-chat send/edit).
 *
 * @returns The sent or edited message object, the array of sent message objects when `chunkSize` selects the chunked reply path, or the {@link IBroadcastSendResult} counts when `broadcast` is present.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleCallbackQueryData() {
 *   // Automatic reply/edit with content from this.template
 *   await this.renderText()
 *
 *   // With keyboard builder and data
 *   const kb = this.inlineKeyboard((k) => k.text("OK", "ok"))
 *   await this.renderText({keyboard: kb, data: {name: "John"}})
 *
 *   // Force a new reply even from a callback query, with a custom base
 *   await this.renderText({keyboard: kb, data: {name: "John"}, AGBaseId: "id-hello-world", mode: "reply"})
 *
 *   // Long message: send in chunks of 4096 characters (keyboard on the last chunk only)
 *   await this.renderText({keyboard: kb, AGBaseId: "id-hello-world", chunkSize: 4096})
 *
 *   // Broadcast: send the block to many users (rich templates send rich)
 *   await this.renderText({data: {name: "John"}, broadcast: {ids: [123456, 789012], languageCode: [`en`, `id`]}})
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Answers a web app query via the Bot API with a caller-built result.
 *
 * Template block: `<g-answer-note>` (read via `getGAnswerNote`).
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Unlike the other answers this carries an explicit query id (there is no
 * context-aware alias — web app queries arrive without an answerable
 * update), mirroring `renderGift`'s explicit target. The result content is
 * built by the caller from `data` (multilang payloads); the `<g-answer-note>`
 * block is resolved as fail-fast validation that the template exists, per
 * the AGBaseId-required policy.
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderGift`): failures are
 * classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`,
 * and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`).
 * After notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.
 *
 * @param params - Answer params: `webAppQueryId` unique identifier for the query to answer (required); `result` inline result built by the caller (required); `data` optional template interpolation data (or null to omit); `AGBaseId` template base ID position, resolved for validation (required); `options` optional abort signal (or null to omit).
 *
 * @returns The sent web app message object.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript

 *   await this.renderWebAppAnswer({webAppQueryId: queryId, result: article, AGBaseId: `webapp-card`})
 * }
 * ```

 * @public
 */

/**
 * Resolve a media `src` through the instance path jail.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Forwards `this.mediaRoots` into `Ctx.resolveMediaInput`. Jail denial is
 * detected by comparing the jailed form against the free form: when the
 * free form would upload (`InputFile`) but the jailed form passes through
 * (`string`), the path was denied and a `log.warn` names the rejected
 * path (never file contents). Null-safe: an absent `log` stays silent.
 *
 * @param src - Template media `src` (file path, `file_id`, URL, or binary payload).
 *
 * @param filename - Optional upload filename forwarded to `resolveMediaInput`.
 *
 * @returns `InputFile` for allowed local files and binary payloads, otherwise `src` unchanged.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: resolveMedia

members.docComment:
/**
 * Resolve a template media `src` into an uploadable value.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * When `src` points at a real local file (`existsSync` + `statSync().isFile()`),
 * it is wrapped in `new InputFile(src, filename)` so grammy uploads it.
 * `file_id` values, URLs, and missing paths pass through unchanged — never throws.
 * Pre-built `InputFile` instances pass through as-is when no `filename` is
 * given; a defined `filename` returns a prototype-preserving clone
 * (`Object.create` + `Object.assign`) so shared caller instances are never
 * mutated. `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` payloads are wrapped in
 * `new InputFile(src, filename)`.
 *
 * Opt-in local-path jail (Q8 option b): when `roots` is a non-empty list,
 * a local file uploads ONLY when its resolved absolute form sits under one
 * of the resolved roots — otherwise it passes through unchanged (sent as a
 * `file_id`, never throws, never uploads). `null`/empty `roots` keeps
 * current behavior unchanged. `file_id`/URL/`Buffer`/`InputFile` sources
 * are unaffected by the jail. Symlink limitation: the check is lexical
 * (`resolve` without `realpath` — see `Ctx.isPathUnderRoots`).
 *
 * @param src - Template media `src` (file path, `file_id`, URL, or binary payload).
 *
 * @param filename - Optional upload filename; overrides `InputFile.filename` on a clone when defined.
 *
 * @param roots - Optional jail roots; `null`/empty disables the jail.
 *
 * @returns `InputFile` for local files and binary payloads, otherwise `src` unchanged.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: resolveMediaInput

 * independent sessions — a private chat and a group must not share pending

 * `:chatId`, which still scopes by chat instead of collapsing every

/**
 * Starts a channel giveaway from a single params object.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Data-driven by design (no `<g-giveaway>` block): `sendGiveaway`
 * has no `parse_mode`, so template interpolation adds no value. Requires
 * the bot to be an administrator in the target channel; the installed
 * grammy exposes no typed `sendGiveaway` (neither `api.` nor `api.raw.`),
 * so this validates fail-fast then sends through a structurally-typed raw
 * call (grammy's raw client dispatches any method name at runtime). Fail-fast validation (1+ channels, future
 * integer `date`, positive integer `winners`, non-empty `prize`) runs
 * BEFORE any API call — programmer errors always throw, never fall back.
 * The first channel receives the giveaway message and doubles as the
 * primary `chats` entry. Channel-targeted by design, so this keeps `api.raw`
 * (context-aware `replyWith*` can only reach the current chat).
 *
 * Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`): failures are
 * classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`, reported to `notifySendError`,
 * and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`).
 * There is no degraded fallback content for giveaways, so after notify+log
 * the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.
 *
 * @param params - Giveaway params `{channels, date, winners, prize}` (or null — throws).
 *
 * @param options - Optional giveaway flags such as `onlyNewMembers` (or null to omit).
 *
 * @returns The sent giveaway message object.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * async handleLaunch() {
 *   await this.startGiveaway({channels: `@mychannel`, date: 1893456000, winners: 2, prize: `iPhone 16`})
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: startGiveaway

 * @remarks

 * Thin passthrough to `api.stopMessageLiveLocation` — no template involved.

/**
 * In-process E2E testing helper — simulates Telegram updates without HTTP.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Provides a lightweight alternative to spinning up a full webhook server
 * for E2E tests. Uses `bot.api.config.use()` to intercept all outbound
 * Bot API calls in memory (0 HTTP, 0 Bun.serve), and injects Telegram
 * Update objects directly via `bot.bot.handleUpdate()`.
 *
 * Attached to `Gramstax.e2e` when the bot is created with `deploy: "test"`.
 * All methods simulate Telegram updates without any HTTP server or port binding.
 *
 * **Typical usage:**
 * ```typescript
 * import {BotCore} from "../src/core/bot"
 *
 * const bot = new BotCore({deploy: "test", token: "test", log: false})
 * const e2e = bot.e2e
 *
 * const responses = await e2e.sendText("/start", {user: {id: 2001}})
 * expect(responses[0]?.body?.text).toContain("Welcome")
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: E2eHelper

/**
 * Main bot framework class for building Telegram bots.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Gramstax provides a page-based routing system for handling Telegram updates.
 * It automatically loads page classes from the file system and routes incoming
 * messages and callbacks to the appropriate handlers.
 *
 * @typeParam ICtx - The context type extending {@link (Ctx:class)}.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import {Gramstax} from "gramstax"
 *
 * const bot = new Gramstax({
 *   token: process.env.BOT_TOKEN!,
 *   deploy: "polling",
 *   log: true
 * })
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: Gramstax

members.docComment:
/**
 * Routes an incoming update to the appropriate page handler.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * The routing follows a strict **priority hierarchy**. When a match is found
 * at any level, the method executes the handler and returns immediately.
 * If no match is found, it falls through to the next level.
 *
 * **Routing Priority (executed in order):**
 *
 * 1. **staticSession** — Session-aware routes, filtered by input type (O(n) lookup)
 *  - Only runs when the user has an active session (`session.method` is set)
 *  - Iterates `routeStaticSession` and matches by `session.method` value
 *  - **Filtered by input type**: only routes whose name ends with `fromListener`
 *  are checked (e.g., callback queries only match `*CallbackQueryData` session routes,
 *  text only matches `*Text`, photo captions only match `*CaptionPhoto`, etc.)
 *  - This prevents cross-type handler misdispatch (e.g., a callback query
 *  accidentally matching `handleSessionFreeText`)
 *  - Example: session with method "7-mypage" → finds `handleSessionFreeText["7-mypage"]`
 *  when `fromListener = "text"`
 *
 * 2. **static** — Exact intent match routes (O(1) lookup)
 *  - Matches exact text/callback data to page intents
 *  - Example: "start" → `handleText()`, "/help" → `handleCommandText()`
 *
 * 3. **staticIntent** — Intent with args routes (O(1) lookup)
 *  - Matches intent prefix when args are present
 *  - Example: "start:123" → `handleArgsCallbackQueryData()`, "/add item" → `handleCommandArgsText()`
 *
 * 4. **dynamicSpesific** — Non-session free handlers (O(n) iteration)
 *  - Runs all `handleFree*` handlers (defined directly on the page, not inherited)
 *  - `handleSessionFree*` variants are NOT dispatched here — they go through id=1
 *  - Example: `handleFreeText()`, `handleFreePhoto()`
 *  - **All matching handlers are executed** (no early return)
 *
 * 5. **dynamic** — Global fallback handlers (O(n) iteration)
 *  - Runs all `handleFree()` handlers from pages that define them
 *  - Last resort when nothing else matches
 *  - **All matching handlers are executed** (no early return)
 *
 * @param ctx - The context instance.
 *
 * @param fromListener - The listener type that triggered the route.
 *
 * @returns A `PageRouteResult` with `state` indicating what happened
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _pageRoutes

members.docComment:
/**
 * Creates a new Gramstax bot instance.
 *
 * @param params - Configuration options. See {@link IGramstaxParams} for all available options.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Polling mode (development, local testing)
 * new Gramstax({token: "BOT_TOKEN", deploy: "polling"})
 *
 * // Webhook mode with Bun's HTTP server
 * new Gramstax({token: "BOT_TOKEN", deploy: "webhook", optionsDeploy: {webhook: {url: "https://example.com/bot", secretToken: "s3cr3t"}}})
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Serverless mode — worker adapter
 * //
 * // The bot does NOT self-host; instead it sets up handlerBotUpdate
 * // for your serverless runtime. Export the handler and let your
 * // platform invoke it per HTTP request.
 *
 * // bot.ts — instantiation
 * const bot = new Gramstax({
 *   token: process.env.BOT_TOKEN!,
 *   deploy: "serverless",
 *   optionsDeploy: {serverless: {"cloudflare-mod": {url: "https://example.com/webhook", secretToken: env.BOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET}}}
 * })
 *
 * // handler.ts — server entry point
 * import {bot} from "./bot"
 *
 * // Bun's built-in HTTP server
 * Bun.serve({
 *   port: 3000,
 *   async fetch(req) {
 *     const url = new URL(req.url)
 *     if (url.pathname === "/webhook") {
 *       // Forward the request to gramstax's handler
 *       return await bot.handlerBotUpdate(req)
 *     }
 *     return new Response("Not found", {status: 404})
 *   }
 * })
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Serverless mode — AWS Lambda
 * //
 * // bot.ts
 * const bot = new Gramstax({
 *   token: process.env.BOT_TOKEN!,
 *   deploy: "serverless",
 *   optionsDeploy: {serverless: {"aws-lambda-async": {url: "https://example.com/webhook", secretToken: process.env.BOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET}}}
 * })
 *
 * // lambda.ts
 * import {bot} from "./bot"
 * import type {APIGatewayProxyEvent, Context} from "aws-lambda"
 *
 * export const handler = async (event: APIGatewayProxyEvent, _ctx: Context) => {
 *   // webhookCallback(bot.bot, "aws-lambda") wraps the raw event
 *   // into a compatible format internally
 *   return await bot.handlerBotUpdate(event)
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // Serverless mode — Cloudflare Workers
 * //
 * // bot.ts
 * const bot = new Gramstax({token: env.BOT_TOKEN, deploy: "serverless", optionsDeploy: {serverless: {"cloudflare-mod": {url: "https://example.com/webhook", secretToken: env.BOT_WEBHOOK_SECRET}}}})
 *
 * // worker.ts
 * import {bot} from "./bot"
 *
 * export default {
 *   async fetch(request: Request) {
 *     const url = new URL(request.url)
 *     if (url.pathname === "/webhook") {
 *       return await bot.handlerBotUpdate(request)
 *     }
 *     return new Response("OK")
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */

/**
 * Builds the params for one page `Ctx`, plus optional app extras.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Only assembly point for `createCtx`: per-update `ct` plus the
 * constructor-built `ctxScope` plus a fresh `temp`. App values (e.g. a
 * database handle) ride in `extra` through the params object, but the
 * `Ctx` constructor does NOT attach them — assign each one explicitly
 * in your subclass constructor so every wiring stays visible and easy
 * to troubleshoot. `extra` keys must not be `ct`/`temp` (thrown here).
 *
 * @param ct - The grammy context for the current update.
 *
 * @param extra - Optional app values forwarded into every page `Ctx`.
 *
 * @typeParam T - App extra fields merged into the returned params.
 *
 * @returns Params for `new Ctx(...)`, shaped as `ICtxParams & T`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   db = new Db()
 *   override buildCtxParams<T extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, never>>(ct: ICt, _extra?: T): ICtxParams & T & {db: Db} {
 *     return super.buildCtxParams(ct, {db: this.db}) as ICtxParams & T & {db: Db}
 *   }
 * }
 * class CtxCore extends Ctx {
 *   declare db: Db
 *   constructor(params: ICtxParams & {db: Db}) {
 *     super(params)
 *     this.db = params.db
 *   }
 * }
 * // inside any page extending CtxCore: this.db — fully typed, zero casts.
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: buildCtxParams

/**
 * Hook called after the bot has started.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Override this method to run post-start logic. The common use case is
 * initializing background workers — long-running tasks that need the bot
 * to be fully alive (scheduled jobs, periodic cleanup, queue processors,
 * cron-like tasks). Unlike `hookBeforeStart` which runs before the bot
 * is up, this hook guarantees the bot is fully started and `this.bot.api`
 * is operational, so any task that needs to make API calls or interact
 * with the bot instance should be started here.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   async hookAfterStart() {
 *     // Init worker thread from sub WorkerThreadInit
 *     await IncrementJob.launchWorker([5000]) // 5s
 *   }
 * }
 * ```

 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookAfterStart

/**

 * @remarks

 *   console.log(`from listener ${data.listenerName}`)

members.docComment:
/**
 * Hook called before the bot starts.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Override this method to run **one-off initialization logic** that must
 * complete before the bot begins dispatching updates — for example,
 * connecting to a database, warming a cache, validating external service
 * credentials, or setting up shared singletons that pages will read from.
 *
 * This hook fires exactly once, after `cacheSession`, `templateManager`,
 * `bot`, and `pages` are initialized, and before polling/webhook/serverless
 * actually begins receiving updates.
 *
 * **Do NOT register middleware here.** Middleware belongs in
 * {@link Gramstax.registerLowPlugin}, which is the dedicated channel for
 * code that should run on every incoming update. `hookBeforeStart` runs
 * once and is the wrong place for per-update logic.
 *
 * For background tasks that need the bot to be alive (cron jobs, periodic
 * cleanup, queue processors), use {@link Gramstax.hookAfterStart} instead.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   async hookBeforeStart() {
 *     // Validate external service credentials before the bot goes live
 *     if (!process.env.REDIS_URL) {
 *       throw new Error(`REDIS_URL is required`)
 *     }
 *     this.log?.info?.(`Verifying external service connection...`)
 *     await pingRedis(process.env.REDIS_URL)
 *     this.log?.success?.(`External services ready`)
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookBeforeStart

members.docComment:
/**
 * Best-effort send-error hook.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Sibling hooks: `hookUpdateError` (dead updates — terminal) and `hookTrace`
 * (every routed update). This one is the recoverable layer: a
 * `fallback-text` send still serves the user, a `retryable` send still
 * throws to your caller. Routing rule: retry-queue ← `hookSendError`,
 * Sentry ← `hookUpdateError`, dashboard ← `hookTrace`.
 *
 * @param err - The send error.
 *
 * @param info - The send-error info (`page`, `kind`, `chatId`). See {@link ISendErrorHook}.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   override hookSendError(err: unknown, info: ISendErrorInfo): void {
 *     // info: {page: `admin/logs`, kind: `fallback-text` | `retryable`, chatId?: number}
 *     if (info.kind === `retryable`) queueRetry(info)
 *     else metrics.count(info.page, info.kind)
 *   }
 * }
 * // Throwing inside the hook is swallowed — the send flow never breaks.
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Retry-for-later: collect retryables, re-drive them from a job.
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   retryQueue: Array<{err: unknown, page: string, chatId?: number, at: number}> = []
 *   override hookSendError(err: unknown, info: ISendErrorInfo): void {
 *     if (info.kind === `retryable`) this.retryQueue.push({err, page: info.page, chatId: info.chatId, at: Date.now()})
 *   }
 * }
 * // NOTE: `retryable` still throws to your caller — the hook only observes.
 * // Drain `retryQueue` from a worker/job; do not retry inline (429 needs backoff).
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 *
 * Severity split: Sentry for retryables, logs for user-caused fallbacks.
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   override hookSendError(err: unknown, info: ISendErrorInfo): void {
 *     if (info.kind === `retryable`) Sentry.captureException(err, {tags: {page: info.page}})
 *     // `fallback-text` (403 blocked, file deleted) is a normal condition — log, don't alert.
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @defaultValue `undefined` (no hook)
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: hookSendError

members.docComment:
/**
 * Optional OTel-style trace export hook.
 *
 * @remarks

 * Sibling hooks: `hookSendError` (per-send failures) and `hookUpdateError`
 * (dead updates). Routing rule: retry-queue ← `hookSendError`,
 * Sentry ← `hookUpdateError`, dashboard ← `hookTrace`.
 *
 * @param span - The trace span with `name`, `durationMs`, and `attributes`.

 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   override hookTrace(span: {name: string; durationMs: number; attributes: Record<string, unknown>}): void {
 *     tracer.export(span)

members.docComment:
/**
 * Returns middleware to register as low-level plugins on the bot.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Override this method in a subclass to inject custom plugin middleware
 * (sessions, i18n, rate limiting, logging, authentication, etc.) into the
 * underlying bot instance.
 *
 * Each element of the returned array is a {@link ICtMiddleware} value (either a
 * `MiddlewareFn` `(ctx, next) => ...` or a `MiddlewareObj` container) that
 * The array elements are passed to `this.bot.use(...)`. It is meant to be
 * spread into `bot.use`, so the order of elements determines the order in
 * which middleware runs — earlier entries wrap later ones (outermost first).
 *
 * Difference vs. the other lifecycle hooks:
 *
 * - `hookBeforeStart` — for one-off side effects before the bot starts.
 *  Anything you want to happen exactly once at boot goes there.
 * - `registerLowPlugin` — for middleware that must run on **every update**.
 *  Use this when you need middleware semantics (filter queries,
 *  `next()` chaining, scope-aware registration).
 * - `hookBeforeRoute` / `hookAfterRoute` — for per-update hooks that run
 *  inside the router, after gramstax has already routed to a page.
 *
 * The base implementation is not provided — subclasses override this to
 * contribute their own plugins. Returning an empty array (or not
 * overriding) installs no plugins, which is the default behavior.
 *
 * @returns Array of {@link ICtMiddleware}
 * values, ready to be spread into `this.bot.use(...result)`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * class MyBot extends Gramstax {
 *   registerLowPlugin() {
 *     return [
 *       // 1. Logging middleware (outermost — runs first, exits last)
 *       async (ctx, next) => {
 *         this.log?.info?.(`update ${ctx.update.update_id} from ${ctx.from?.id}`)
 *         await next()
 *       },
 *       // 2. Per-chat rate limit (inner)
 *       async (ctx, next) => {
 *         // ... check + throttle ...
 *         await next()
 *       }
 *     ]
 *   }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * @virtual @public
 */
members.name: registerLowPlugin

/**

 *
 * Full page data with typed `callbackQueryData` according to the args
 * configured via `buildData`. Every page SHOULD define `static data`
 * via `buildData(...)` to enable callback query routing.

 * is accepted as-is and the route is only resolved at runtime.

 * never forwards `params.type` to `_broadcastSendMedia` — the kind is read from

 * therefore honours the wrapper's fixed kind.

 * the update carries a `callbackQuery`, `reply` always sends, `edit` always
 * edits. `options` feeds the reply branch and the `editMessageMedia` error
 * state; `optionsEdit1`/`optionsEdit2` feed the edit branch only and are

 * send loop (`type` optional — the kind is read from the template), and
 * `broadcast.targets` runs the revise loop (`type` required). `mode`,
 * `fallbackEdit`, and the `options*` fields do not apply to the send loop.
 * The per-kind wrappers accept only the revise loop — see
 * {@link IRenderMediaKindParams}.
 *
 * @typeParam T - The media type (photo, video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location, contact).

/**
 * Synchronously load all page modules from a directory.
 *
 * Supports both flat `.ts`/`.js` files and subfolder `index.ts`/`index.js`
 * entries. In a subfolder, **any** `.ts`/`.js` file (not just `index`) is
 * recognised as a page — its route name becomes `parentDir/basename`. A
 * file `help.ts` is equivalent to `help/index.ts`; using both simultaneously
 * produces a duplicate error. Nesting can be arbitrary deep.
 *
 * Supported cases and extensions:
 * - Extensions: `.ts` and `.js` only — other files are ignored.
 * - Flat file: `start.ts` → route `start`.
 * - Nested file: `admin/ban.ts` → route `admin/ban` (arbitrary depth).
 * - Directory index: `admin/index.ts` → route `admin`.
 * - A root-level `index.ts`/`index.js` has no parent route and is rejected
 *  with an empty-routeName error — rename it to a named file instead.
 *
 * @param path - Path to the pages directory. Uses default pages directory when omitted.
 *
 * @param positionModule - Index of the exported class. Used when files have multiple exports. Defaults to `0`.
 *
 * @returns Array of page records containing `path`, `page` and `routeName` properties.
 *
 * @throws
 *
 * Error if directory does not exist.
 *
 * @throws
 *
 * Error if a file and a directory-index share the same route name.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const pages = PageManager.getFileManySync();
 * // => [
 * //   { path: "/path/to/start.ts",          page: StartPage,   routeName: "start" },
 * //   { path: "/path/to/settings.ts",       page: SettingsPage, routeName: "settings" },
 * //   { path: "/path/to/start/help.ts",     page: HelpPage,    routeName: "start/help" },
 * //   { path: "/path/to/start/help/index.ts", page: HelpPage,  routeName: "start/help" },
 * //                                        ↑ identical route — duplicate error if both exist
 * // ]
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: getFileManySync

members.docComment:
/**
 * Resolve the concurrency-gate key for an update.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Layered, narrowest-resource-first. The gate exists because session writes are
 * last-write-wins with no compare-and-swap, so two updates touching the same
 * logical resource must never run at once.
 *
 * 1. `chat.id` — all traffic for one chat serializes regardless of sender.
 * 2. `from.id` — chat-less user-originated updates (`inline_query`,
 *  `chosen_inline_result`, `poll_answer`, `join_request`, `my_chat_member`,
 *  `chat_member`, `chat_join_request`, and `callback_query` without a message).
 *  For an anonymous poll voter `poll_answer.voter_chat.id` stands in.
 * 3. `update_id` — globally unique, so each such update gets a private slot.
 *  This degrades to "no serialization" rather than over-serializing unrelated
 *  updates against each other.
 *
 * Note: `poll` carries no actor — Bot API 7.0 removed `Poll.user`, so a poll
 * change reaches this function's step 3 and gets a private slot.
 *
 * Returns `undefined` only when the update carries no `update_id`, in which case
 * the caller must not gate it.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: resolveGateKey

members.docComment:

members.docComment:
/**
 * Static utility class for parsing and compiling HTML-like templates.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * The `TemplateEngine` provides methods for parsing HTML-like template syntax
 * with custom blocks (base, message, keyboard, media, description, etc.) and
 * compiling them into executable functions. It supports variable interpolation,
 * conditional rendering, array mapping, script execution, and template imports.
 *
 * Templates are typically organized into `<g-base>` blocks containing various
 * content blocks like `<g-message>`, `<g-keyboard>`, `<g-media>`, and `<g-description>`.
 * Each block supports a `lang` attribute for internationalization.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import { TemplateEngine } from 'gramstax';
 *
 * const template = `
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-keyboard>Back, Next</g-keyboard>
 *     <g-message>Welcome {{name}}!</g-message>
 *   </g-base>
 * `;
 *
 * const messages = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGMessages(template);
 * const keyboards = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGKeyboards(template);
 *
 * const msg = messages.default?.default?.({ name: 'John' });
 * // Result: {text: 'Welcome John!', rich: false}
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: TemplateEngine

members.docComment:
/**
 * AOT collect hook: when set, `_compileToFunction` records the body and
 * returns a tagged stub instead of calling `new Function`.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Build tooling only (`AotEmitter` installs it around compilation and
 * always uninstalls in `finally`). `undefined` (default) runs the exact
 * JIT path — no behavior change.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: __emitHook

members.docComment:
/**
 * AOT link hook: when set, `_compileToFunction` returns the pre-registered
 * inline function matching the body instead of calling `new Function`.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Edge-runtime path (`AotEmitter` output): emitted modules pre-register
 * every collected body, then rebuild wrapper blocks through the normal
 * compilers with this hook resolving hits. A miss throws (template drift —
 * regenerate). Never set together with `__emitHook`.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: __linkHook

members.docComment:
/**
 * Builds the JavaScript function body for a processed template.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Runs the three structural pre-processors in a fixed order — script blocks,
 * then `<g-div>`, then `<g-space>` — before converting the result to a
 * concatenation expression. The body is returned as source text, never
 * evaluated here: `_compileToFunction` is what turns it into a callable.
 *
 * @param template - Processed template source, or one source per language
 * when `isArray` is `true`.
 *
 * @param isArray - When `true`, emit a body returning `string[]`.
 *
 * @returns The `return` statement source for the compiled function.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _buildFunctionBody

members.docComment:
/**
 * Applies `|filter:arg` pipes to an already-resolved head expression.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Split out of {@link TemplateEngine._processScopeVariables} so `<g-map>` can run the
 * same whitelist over its own loop variables instead of re-deriving the pipe grammar.
 * The caller resolves the head — a `data` path or a loop variable — and passes the whole
 * expression; the leading segment is dropped because it is already baked into `access`.
 *
 * @param access - JavaScript expression for the head, e.g. `(data?.user)` or `(e.name)`
 *
 * @param expr - The full expression including its head segment, used for the warning text
 *
 * @param warned - Filter names already reported, so each unknown filter warns once
 *
 * @returns The chained call, or `""` when a filter is not on the whitelist
 */
members.name: _compileFilterChain

members.docComment:
/**
 * Wraps a compiled string `src` fn so bare placeholders pass objects by reference.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Strings, `null`, and `undefined` fall through to the existing compiled fn
 * (byte-identical output, same escaping and `''` fallback). Non-string
 * values (pre-built `InputFile`, `Buffer`, `Uint8Array`) bypass stringify
 * and reach grammY intact.
 *
 * @param rawSrc - Raw `src` attribute value from the parsed template.
 *
 * @param stringFn - Existing compiled string renderer for this `src`.
 *
 * @returns Renderer yielding either the string output or the raw object.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _compileMediaSrc

members.docComment:
/**
 * Compiles a processed template body into a callable renderer.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Three mutually exclusive paths, in priority order: `__linkHook` resolves
 * a pre-registered body (the AOT link phase, used by edge output with no
 * `Function` constructor), `__emitHook` records the body and returns a
 * stub (the AOT collect phase), otherwise the body is compiled through
 * `new Function` — the exact JIT path taken when neither hook is set.
 *
 * The compiled renderer closes over `_escapeData` and `DEFAULT_FILTERS`, so
 * callers pass only `data`. `isArray` selects the return shape: `string[]`
 * for media-group style templates, `string` otherwise.
 *
 * @param template - Processed template source, or one source per language
 * when `isArray` is `true`.
 *
 * @param isArray - When `true`, compile to a renderer returning `string[]`.
 *
 * @returns A renderer taking `data` and returning the compiled output.
 *
 * @throws
 *
 * Error when `__linkHook` and `__emitHook` are both set, which would
 * confuse the AOT collect and link phases.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _compileToFunction

members.docComment:
/**
 * Escapes special characters in a string for safe use in template literals.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method escapes backslashes, backticks, and `${` sequences to
 * prevent static template text from breaking out of template literal syntax
 * during compilation. Applied to static segments before they are embedded in
 * generated code (`_compileToFunction` builds concatenation, never raw
 * backtick-wrapped statics; block processors escape embedded content).
 *
 * @param str - The input string to escape
 *
 * @returns The escaped string with backslashes and backticks properly escaped
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const escaped = TemplateEngine._escape('Hello `world`');
 * // Result: 'Hello \\`world\\`'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _escape

members.docComment:
/**
 * HTML-escapes a runtime value for safe interpolation into rich-HTML messages.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Non-string values are stringified; `null`/`undefined` become empty string.
 * Escaped code points: `&` → `&`, `<` → `<`, `>` → `>`.
 * Scope: text-node interpolation via `{{}}` only. Attribute values and
 * `{{{}}}` raw output are intentionally not HTML-escaped.
 *
 * @param value - The runtime value to escape.
 *
 * @returns The escaped string.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _escapeData

members.docComment:
/**
 * Escapes static template text while preserving template syntax spans.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Walks `content` char-by-char: `{{{...}}}`, `{{...}}`, and `{~...~}`
 * spans pass through untouched (they are converted to generated code
 * later). A balanced `${...}` span is preserved live only when its inner
 * code passes {@link TemplateEngine._isGeneratedCode} — i.e. it was
 * produced by an inner block processor (nested `<g-map>` bodies carry
 * `${(() => ...)}` / `${__esc(...)}` spans through outer escaping).
 * Any other `${` sequence (untrusted/static text, unterminated spans)
 * is neutralized via {@link TemplateEngine._escape}, consistent with
 * top-level static text. Every other character goes through
 * {@link TemplateEngine._escape}, neutralizing breakout payloads
 * (backticks, backslashes) in untrusted static text. Used by
 * `_processGSwitchBlocks` and `_processGMapBlocks` for case/default and
 * loop bodies.
 *
 * @param content - Raw static block content to escape.
 *
 * @returns The content with non-syntax characters escaped.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _escapeStaticExceptInterpolation

members.docComment:
/**
 * Extracts specific blocks from template content with optional filtering.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method extracts content from templates based on base ID,
 * block type, language, and section mode. It supports scoped extraction
 * with indentation normalization for clean output.
 *
 * @param content - The template content to extract from
 *
 * @param blocks - Block type(s) to extract, or `"all"` for all blocks
 *
 * @param AGBaseId - The base ID to extract from (defaults to `"default"`)
 *
 * @param section - Whether to return the full block (`"all"`) or just inner content (`"value"`)
 *
 * @param lang - Optional language filter for blocks
 *
 * @returns The extracted content as a string
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = `
 *   <g-base id="main">
 *     <g-message>Hello</g-message>
 *     <g-keyboard>Yes, No</g-keyboard>
 *   </g-base>
 * `;
 * const result = TemplateEngine._extractBlock(template, 'message', 'main', 'value');
 * // Result: 'Hello'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _extractBlock

members.docComment:
/**
 * Extracts lowercase block tag names from an iterable of tag literals.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Strips leading `</` or `<`, any trailing `>`, any attributes that follow
 * a space, and lowercases the result. Self-closing tags like `<g-import/>`
 * are normalised to their bare name. Entries with attributes after a space
 * (e.g. `<blockquote expandable>`) are returned with the attribute suffix
 * preserved.
 *
 * @param blocks - Iterable of tag literals (e.g. `["<g-base>", "<message/>", "<blockquote expandable>"]`)
 *
 * @returns Set of normalized lowercase block names
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const names = TemplateEngine._extractBlockNames([
 *   "<g-base>",
 *   "<g-import/>",
 *   "<BLOCKQUOTE expandable>"
 * ]);
 * // => Set { "g-base", "g-import", "blockquote expandable" }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _extractBlockNames

members.docComment:
/**
 * Identifiers that `<g-ifelse>` never rewrites to `data?.x`.

 * @remarks

 * Three groups: reserved words that cannot be references, the parameter names every
 * compiled template body already has in scope (`data`, `__esc`, `FILTERS`), and the
 * standard globals a template author may legitimately call.

members.docComment:
/**
 * Collects the parameter names introduced by every arrow function in a token list.

 * @remarks

 * A conditional body may contain `items.filter((item) => item.on).length > 0`. Those
 * parameters are locals, not scope reads, and must survive the rewrite untouched.
 *
 * @param tokens - Output of {@link TemplateEngine._tokenizeExpression}

 * @returns The local names, valid for the whole expression

members.name: _ifelseArrowLocals

members.docComment:
/**
 * Reports whether a `<g-ifelse>` body actually branches.

 * @remarks
 *
 * `<g-ifelse>` exists for conditionals only, so a body with no ternary and no
 * short-circuit operator is rejected rather than silently becoming an `{~~}` clone.

 * @param tokens - Output of {@link TemplateEngine._tokenizeExpression}

 * @returns True when the body contains `?:`, `&&`, `||`, or `??`

members.name: _isConditionalExpression

members.docComment:
/**
 * Compiles a processed template string into an executable function.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method takes a pre-processed template (or array of templates)
 * and compiles it into a JavaScript function that accepts a `data` object and
 * returns the rendered result. The function is created using `new Function()`.
 * Static segments are emitted via string concatenation (`JSON.stringify`
 * literals joined with `+`), never wrapped in a raw backtick literal, so
 * static backticks, backslashes, and `${` sequences cannot break out into
 * code. Only `${...}` spans produced by the block/scope processors are
 * evaluated.
 *
 * @param template - The processed template string or array of strings
 *
 * @param isArray - Whether the template parameter is an array
 *
 * @typeParam T - Boolean type indicating whether the input is an array
 *
 * @returns A function that accepts optional data and returns the rendered string or string array
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const processed = '${(data && data["name"]) ?? ""}';
 * const fn = TemplateEngine._compileToFunction(processed, false);
 * const result = fn({ name: 'John' });
 * // Result: 'John'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _isGeneratedCode

members.docComment:
/**
 * Decides whether a `{` opens an object literal (keys are not scope reads) or a block.
 *
 * @param tokens - Output of {@link TemplateEngine._tokenizeExpression}

 * @param index - Index of the `{` token
 *
 * @returns True when the brace opens an object literal
 */
members.name: _isObjectLiteralBrace

members.docComment:
/**
 * Matches a bare `src` placeholder with no pipes or surrounding text.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Only `{{dotted.path}}` (optional surrounding whitespace) qualifies —
 * filtered (`{{x|upper}}`) or embedded (`pre-{{x}}`) values keep the
 * existing string pipeline untouched.
 *
 * @param rawSrc - Raw `src` attribute value from the parsed template.
 *
 * @returns Dotted path when bare, otherwise `null`.
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _matchBareMediaPlaceholder

members.docComment:
/**
 * Attribute value validators for `<g-*>` PAGE blocks.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Per-tag, per-attribute map of validators. Each validator receives the
 * raw attribute value (after quote-stripping) and returns either `null`
 * (valid) or a descriptive error string. The value validation runs after
 * the per-block attribute validation, so unknown attributes are reported
 * separately by `validateBlockG*Attributes` methods.
 *
 * Currently covers:
 * - `<g-base id>` — must not be empty
 * - `<g-keyboard type>` — must be `inline` or `bottom`
 * - `<g-media type>` — must be one of: photo, video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location, contact
 * - `<g-media shared>` — must be `true` or `false`
 * - `<g-media filename>` — any string, always valid
 * - `<g-poll type>` — must be `regular` or `quiz`
 * - `<g-poll correct>` — must be a non-negative option index
 * - `<g-poll explanation>` — any string, always valid
 * - `<g-poll anonymous>` / `<g-poll multiple>` — must be `true` or `false`
 * - `<g-venue title>` / `<g-venue address>` — any string, always valid
 * - `<g-venue latitude>` — must be a number between -90 and 90; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced)
 * - `<g-venue longitude>` — must be a number between -180 and 180; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced)
 * - `<g-dice emoji>` — must be one of 🎲🎯🏀⚽🎳🎰; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced)
 * - `<g-invoice currency>` — must be a 3-letter code (`XTR` or fiat); `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced)
 * - `<g-price amount>` — must be a positive integer in smallest currency units
 * - `<g-paid-media stars>` — must be a positive integer 1–25000; `{{}}` values skip the static check (runtime-enforced)
 *
 * Validators are intentionally lenient — they catch obvious bugs (wrong
 * type, invalid value) but do not enforce every framework-level constraint.
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * TemplateEngine._PAGE_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS["g-keyboard"].type("inline")   // => null
 * TemplateEngine._PAGE_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS["g-keyboard"].type("sidebar") // => "Attribute \"type\" on <g-keyboard> must be \"inline\" or \"bottom\", got \"sidebar\""
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _PAGE_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS

/**
 * Block: g-media
 * Extracts and parses `<g-media>` blocks from a template string.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method identifies all `<g-media>` blocks and extracts their
 * attributes and content. It supports various media types including photo,
 * video, audio, document, animation, voice, video_note, sticker, location,
 * and contact. The inner content becomes the caption for supported types.
 *
 * **Attributes:**
 *  - `lang` (optional): Language key for the output map. Defaults to `"default"`.
 *  - `type` (required): Media type discriminator. Expected values:
 *  - `photo`, `video`, `audio`, `document`, `animation`, `voice`, `video_note`,
 *  - `sticker`, `location`, `contact`.
 *  - `src` (optional): File path / URL / file identifier for file-based media.
 *  - `latitude` (optional): Location latitude (used when `type="location"`).
 *  - `longitude` (optional): Location longitude (used when `type="location"`).
 *  - `phone` (optional): Contact phone number (used when `type="contact"`).
 *  - `first_name` (optional): Contact first name (used when `type="contact"`).
 *  - `last_name` (optional): Contact last name (used when `type="contact"`).
 *  - `vcard` (optional): Contact vCard payload (used when `type="contact"`).
 *
 * Media rules (based on `type`):
 * - If `src` exists, it is assigned as `mediaBlock.src` (for any type).
 * - If `src` contains pipe-delimited values, `mediaBlock.srcList` is populated
 *  with up to 10 trimmed entries for Telegram media groups.
 * - If caption exists and `type !== "video_note"` and `type !== "sticker"`,
 *  it is assigned as `mediaBlock.caption`.
 * - If `type === "location"`, `latitude` and `longitude` are copied if present,
 *  and caption (if present) is also allowed.
 * - If `type === "contact"`, `phone`, `first_name`, `last_name`, and `vcard`
 *  are copied if present, and caption (if present) is also allowed.
 *
 * Note:
 * - If multiple `<g-media>` blocks share the same `lang`, the last one wins
 *  (it overwrites the previous entry).
 *
 * @param template - The template string containing `<g-media>` blocks
 *
 * @returns An object mapping language keys to their corresponding media block configurations
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = '<g-media type="photo" src="image.jpg|image-2.jpg" lang="en">Hello</g-media>';
 * const media = TemplateEngine._processGMediaBlocks(template);
 * // Result: { en: { type: 'photo', src: 'image.jpg|image-2.jpg', srcList: ['image.jpg', 'image-2.jpg'], caption: 'Hello' } }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _processGMediaBlocks

 * Transforms `<g-script>` blocks into executable JavaScript expressions.

 * @remarks
 *
 * This internal method converts `<g-script>` blocks into self-invoking functions
 * that execute with access to the `data` object via `with(data)`. If the script
 * throws an error or `data` is undefined, an empty string is returned.
 * By design this executes developer-authored template code (templates are
 * code, only `data` values are untrusted input); no strict/no-script mode
 * is provided.

 * @param template - The template string containing `<g-script>` blocks

 * @returns The template with `<g-script>` blocks converted to executable expressions
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript

/**
 * Compiles keyboard blocks from a template into executable functions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method parses `<g-keyboard>` blocks from the template and compiles them
 * into functions that generate button label arrays. The result is organized by
 * base ID and language, with separate `inline` and `bottom` keyboard modes.
 * Comma-separated labels are split into individual button strings.
 *
 * Processing pipeline (in order, per keyboard label):
 * 1. `_processGScriptBlocks` – converts `<g-script>` blocks into executable expressions
 * 2. `_processGMapBlocks` – converts `<g-map>` blocks into array map expressions
 * 3. `_processGSwitchBlocks` – converts `<g-switch>` blocks into switch expressions
 * 4. `_processScopeExec` – evaluates scope execution blocks (implementation-defined)
 * 5. `_processScopeVariables` – resolves scope variables (implementation-defined)
 * 6. `_compileToFunction(processedLabels, true)` – produces the final render function
 *
 * Notes:
 * - Keyboard content is split by commas into individual labels.
 * - Escaped commas with double backslash (`\\,`) are preserved as literal commas.
 * - Each label is processed independently through the pipeline.
 *
 * Output shape:
 * - First level key: `AGBaseId` (from `<g-base id="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted)
 * - Second level key: `ALang` (from `<g-keyboard lang="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted)
 * - Third level key: `mode`:
 *  - `inline` (default)
 *  - `bottom`
 * - Value: `(data?: Record<string, unknown>) => string[]`
 *
 * @param template - Raw template string containing `<g-base>` and `<g-keyboard>` blocks
 *
 * @param gBaseBlocks - Optional pre-parsed base blocks for reuse
 *
 * @returns Compiled keyboard functions organized by base ID, language, and mode
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = `
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-keyboard>Yes, No, {{action}}</g-keyboard>
 *     <g-keyboard type="bottom">Menu, Help</g-keyboard>
 *   </g-base>
 * `;
 * const keyboards = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGKeyboards(template);
 * const inline = keyboards.default?.default?.inline?.({ action: 'Cancel' });
 * // Result: ['Yes', 'No', 'Cancel']
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: _splitKeyboardLabels

 * @remarks

/**
 * Attribute value validators for Telegram Rich HTML tags.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Per-tag, per-attribute map of validators. Each validator receives the
 * raw attribute value (after quote-stripping) and returns either `null`
 * (valid) or a descriptive error string. The value validation runs after
 * the required-attribute check, so missing attributes are reported
 * separately by {@link TemplateEngine._TELEGRAM_REQUIRED_ATTRS}.

 * Options spec (see `BOT_API_VERSION`). `{{placeholder}}` values and
 * boolean attributes (no `=value`) are skipped by the caller.

 * TemplateEngine._TELEGRAM_ATTR_VALUE_VALIDATORS["tg-time"].unix("abc")       // => "unix must be a positive integer (got \"abc\")"

 * @remarks

/**
 * Splits a `<g-ifelse>` body into tokens so identifiers can be rewritten without a
 * JavaScript parser dependency.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Token types: `word`, `number`, `string`, `template`, `regex`, `punct`. Whitespace and
 * comments are dropped — spacing is not preserved because the output is re-emitted source.
 *
 * Two constructs are tokenized as opaque single tokens and therefore never rewritten:
 * regex literals, and template literals (so `${...}` inside them cannot be silently
 * reinterpreted). Template literals that do carry `${` interpolation are rejected by
 * {@link TemplateEngine.validateBlockGIfElseBody} rather than mis-rewritten here.
 *
 * A `/` is read as division when the previous token can end a value (word, number, string,
 * template, `)`, `]`, `++`, `--`) and as a regex literal otherwise. This is the standard
 * heuristic and is ambiguous for `if (x) /re/.test(s)`; it resolves toward division, which
 * is the common case in a template conditional.
 *
 * @param expr - The raw `<g-ifelse>` body
 *
 * @returns The token list

members.docComment:
/**
 * Registry of supported scope interpolation syntaxes.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * These are the variable/expression delimiters recognized within template content.
 * Each entry represents a pair of opening/closing delimiters that trigger a specific
 * interpolation behavior at compile time.
 *
 * **Supported scopes:**
 * - `{{}}` — Mustache-style variable interpolation. Placeholders like `{{name}}` are
 *  replaced with the corresponding value from the `data` object at render time.
 *  Nullish values produce an empty string.
 * - `{~~}` — Inline execution blocks. Expressions like `{~ status ? "Success" : "Failed" ~}` are
 *  evaluated as JavaScript expressions with access to the `data` object.
 *
 * This array is used for reference/documentation purposes; the actual parsing is
 * handled by `_processScopeVariables` (for `{{}}`) and `_processScopeExec` (for `{~~}`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * console.log(TemplateEngine.ALLOWED_SCOPE)
 * // Result: ['{{}}', '{~~}']
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: ALLOWED_SCOPE

/**
 * Compiles description blocks from a template into executable functions.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method parses `<g-description>` blocks from the template and compiles them
 * into functions that generate rendered description strings. The result is organized
 * by base ID, scope, and language. Used for Telegram bot command descriptions.
 *
 * Processing pipeline (in order, per description):
 * 1. `_processGScriptBlocks` – converts `<g-script>` blocks into executable expressions
 * 2. `_processGMapBlocks` – converts `<g-map>` blocks into array map expressions
 * 3. `_processGSwitchBlocks` – converts `<g-switch>` blocks into switch expressions
 * 4. `_processScopeExec` – evaluates scope execution blocks (implementation-defined)
 * 5. `_processScopeVariables` – resolves scope variables (implementation-defined)
 * 6. `_compileToFunction(processed, false)` – produces the final render function
 *
 * Output shape:
 * - First level key: `AGBaseId` (from `<g-base id="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted)
 * - Second level key: `AScope` (from `<g-description scope="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted)
 * - Third level key: `ALang` (from `<g-description lang="...">`, or `"default"` if omitted)
 * - Value: `(data?: Record<string, unknown>) => string`
 *
 * @param template - Raw template string containing `<g-base>` and `<g-description>` blocks
 *
 * @param gBaseBlocks - Optional pre-parsed base blocks for reuse
 *
 * @returns Compiled description functions organized by base ID, scope, and language
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = `
 *   <g-base>
 *     <g-description>Start the bot</g-description>
 *     <g-description scope="chat_administrators">Admin command</g-description>
 *   </g-base>
 * `;
 * const descriptions = TemplateEngine.compileBlockGDescription(template);

 * // Result: 'Start the bot'
 * ```

 * @public

members.docComment:
/**
 * Recursively processes and resolves `<g-import>` blocks in a template.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * This method resolves all `<g-import>` placeholders produced by `_processGImportBlocks` by invoking a user-provided `resolver` function.
 *
 * Resolution behavior:
 * - Each `<g-import>` is resolved by calling `resolver(src)` to obtain raw template content.
 * - The resolved content is filtered using `_extractBlock` based on the import metadata
 *  (`blocks`, `base`, `section`, `lang`).
 * - If the resolved content itself contains `<g-import>` directives, they are processed
 *  recursively.
 *
 * Recursion and safety:
 * - Recursive import resolution is limited to a maximum depth of **10** to prevent
 *  infinite import loops.
 * - If the depth limit is exceeded, an empty string is returned.
 *
 * Output behavior:
 * - `<g-import>` placeholders (`__IMPORT_N__`) are replaced sequentially.
 * - If the resolver returns `null` or an empty result, the import is replaced with
 *  an empty string.
 *
 * @param template - Template string containing `<g-import>` directives
 *
 * @param resolver - Function that resolves import sources to template content
 *
 * @param depth - Current recursion depth (defaults to 0)
 *
 * @param importCache - Optional Map to cache resolved imports for reuse
 *
 * @returns Template with all `<g-import>` blocks resolved and replaced
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const template = '<g-import src="header" block="message" />\n<g-message>Main content</g-message>';
 * const resolver = (src: string) => {
 *   if (src === 'header') return '<g-message>Header text</g-message>';
 *   return null;
 * };
 * const result = TemplateEngine.processGImportBlocks(template, resolver);
 * // Result: '<g-message>Header text</g-message>\n<g-message>Main content</g-message>'
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: processGImportBlocks

members.docComment:
/**
 * Validates the body of every `<g-ifelse>` block.
 *
 * @remarks
 *
 * Four rules, all required to keep the block a conditional and unambiguous:
 *
 * 1. The body must not be empty.
 * 2. `{{}}` and `{~~}` interpolation must not appear — the body is already JavaScript, and
 *  nesting the interpolation syntaxes inside it would give one construct two grammars.
 * 3. Template literals must not interpolate `${...}` — that is a third spelling of the same
 *  interpolation. Use string concatenation inside the conditional instead.
 * 4. The body must actually branch: a ternary, or a `&&` / `||` / `??` short-circuit.
 *  A plain expression such as `items.length` belongs in `{~~}` and is rejected here so
 *  `<g-ifelse>` cannot silently become a second `{~~}`.
 *
 * @param template - The raw template string to validate
 *
 * @returns An object with a `valid` boolean and an `errors` array
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * TemplateEngine.validateBlockGIfElseBody(`<g-ifelse>items.length</g-ifelse>`);
 * // Result: { valid: false, errors: [{ line: 1, message: '<g-ifelse> body must be a conditional expression — use a ternary (test ? a : b) or a short-circuit (&&, ||, ??), got "items.length". Use {~~ items.length ~~} for a plain expression' }] }
 * ```
 *
 * @public
 */
members.name: validateBlockGIfElseBody
